description: Former BOAC and British Airtours aircraft delivered as G-APFL, registered to Coastal Airways in 1981 but never operated. Airhistory caption of a March 2014 photograph describes it as preserved in the Aero Beach Club garden. The old British registration shows through the paint; the last legal identity was the Ugandan government one.
Former Alitalia Caravelle. Spottingmode notes the last registration may have been 9Q-CRU. Preserved among the Aero Beach display line.
Ex-Russian civil heavy-lift helicopter preserved in the Aero Beach grounds.
Former Uganda Air Force basic trainer. Only the rear fuselage survives at Aero Beach.
Uganda Air Force jet trainer preserved at Aero Beach. A second Ugandan L-29 U-107 is at Soroti and is not part of this site.
Former Uganda Air Force fighter in the Aero Beach line. A second unidentified MiG-17F at the same site is debris only and is not recorded.
Uganda Air Force two-seat conversion trainer at Aero Beach.

Uganda Air Force fighter at Aero Beach. Spottingmode records it as dumped rather than presented and notes the construction number is variously reported as 96009911 and 96010001.
Uganda Air Force fighter at Aero Beach. Construction number confirmed as 9909 by a Spottingmode contributor from the airframe.
Uganda Air Force fighter at Aero Beach now split into two sections. Identified from the construction number 10001 stamped in the wheel bay because no serial survives on the airframe.
